message.content:
I don’t have the ability to pull live data from the internet, so I can’t give you the exact Air Quality Index (AQI) for Los Angeles at this moment.  

If you’d like the most up‑to‑date reading, you can check one of the following resources:

| Service | How to use |
|---------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the current AQI and pollutant breakdown. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and see the latest AQI, forecast, and health recommendations. |
| **Weather apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or smartphone weather widgets) display a local AQI when you search for Los Angeles. |

Typical values for Los Angeles vary seasonally, but during the summer months the city often reports an AQI ranging from **moderate (50–100)** to **unhealthy for sensitive groups (101–150)**, especially on days with high ozone or particulate matter. In winter, the AQI can sometimes dip into the **good (0–50)** range, though traffic and industrial emissions still contribute to moderate levels.

If you’re planning outdoor activities or have respiratory concerns, it’s a good idea to check the current AQI and any health advisories before heading out.
